catalog_quote: The phonological word is closely related to grammatical word classes and can be devided into major and minor phonological words. Major phonological words correspond to noun and verb roots. The word, whether major or minor, is the unit of stress placement. The distribution of stress is conditioned by 1. tone - the syllable with the highest tone bears stress; 2. position - if several syllables bear the same tone and no other tone in the word is higher, then stress falls on the first of these syllables. ... Major phonological words are further marked by potential pause, while minor phonological words cannot stand alone. ... Each syllable carries one of three contrastive level tones: high, mid, low. ... new_statements.rule_in_words: Zulgo is a three-level tone language (H, M, L). Word stress is non-contrastive and predictable from tone: within the phonological word (major = noun/verb root, or minor word), stress falls on the syllable bearing the highest tone; if two or more syllables tie for the highest tone, the leftmost of them is stressed. No fixed positional default independent of tone is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the rule applies to both major and minor phonological words. Words have 1-5 syllables, disyllables most common (sec. 8.1).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (closely matching the grammatical word; major words = noun and verb roots, bounded by potential pause). Downstep and intonation are utterance-level (sec. 7.3, 9). Description based on the Zulgo dialect as spoken at Tala-Zulgo (fieldwork 1976-77).
new_statements.identity_note: Haller 1980 describes the Zulgo dialect [zulgwa] (fieldwork at Tala-Zulgo, speakers from that area), i.e. the Zulgo half of Glottolog's Zulgo-Gemzek (zulg1242; Glottolog lists Zulgo/Gemzek/Mineo as dialects). Haller names Gemjek and Mineo as the other two dialects; Gravina (2003, 2005) treats Gemzek as a distinct language with a substantially different vowel system, so the tone-conditioned stress rule is attested first-hand for Zulgo proper only.

sources.note: Section 8 'The phonological word' (printed p.76 = PDF p.80): the word is the unit of stress placement; stress is conditioned by (1) tone - the syllable with the highest tone bears stress, (2) position - if several syllables share the highest tone, stress falls on the first of them. Section 7 (p.68): three contrastive level tones (high, mid, low), downstep at utterance level. Stress is thus non-contrastive and derived from tone.
